translationRepairs: Her eldest brother, Marquis Lü of Zhou, died on campaign. His son Lü Tai was enfeoffed as Marquis of Li, and his son Zichan as Marquis of Jiao;
Her eldest brother, Marquis Lü of Zhou, died on campaign. His son Lü Tai was enfeoffed as Marquis of Li, and his son Chan as Marquis of Jiao;
In 子產為交侯, 子 means son and 產 is the given name (Lü Chan), not the fused personal name Zichan.

The remainder were all Emperor Xiaohui's younger brothers. Concubine Qi's son Ruyi was the King of Zhao. Lady Bo's son Heng was the King of Dai. The other consorts' sons were Zihui, King of Liang; Ziyou, King of Huaiyang; Zichang, King of Huainan; and Zijian, King of Yan.

The remainder were all Emperor Xiaohui's younger brothers. Concubine Qi's son Ruyi was the King of Zhao. Lady Bo's son Heng was the King of Dai. The other consorts' sons were Hui, King of Liang; You, King of Huaiyang; Chang, King of Huainan; and Jian, King of Yan.
In 子恢/子友/子長/子建, 子 means son; given names are 恢/友/長/建. Zihui-style forms incorrectly fuse kinship 子 into the name.
At dawn, Emperor Xiaohui returned. The King of Zhao was already dead.
By dawn, Emperor Xiaohui had returned; the King of Zhao was already dead.
犁明 marks the coming of dawn as the frame when Xiaohui returned to find Ruyi already dead.
On xinchou in the ninth month, she was buried.
On xinchou in the ninth month, he was buried.
The subject of 葬 after 孝惠帝崩 is Emperor Xiaohui (male), not the empress dowager.
She enfeoffed Zizhang, a son of King Daohui of Qi, as Marquis of Zhuxu and married Lu Lu's daughter to him.
She enfeoffed Zhang, a son of King Daohui of Qi, as Marquis of Zhuxu and married Lü Lu's daughter to him.
In 子章, 子 means son and 章 is the given name; Zizhang incorrectly fuses kinship 子 into the name. Also 呂祿 is Lü Lu, not Lu Lu.

In the fourth year, she enfeoffed Lü Kui as Marquis of Linguang, Lü Ta as Marquis of Yu, Lü Gengshi as Marquis of Zhuiji, Lü Fen as Marquis of Lücheng, and also enfeoffed five chancellors as marquises.

In the fourth year, she enfeoffed Lü Xu as Marquis of Linguang, Lü Ta as Marquis of Yu, Lü Gengshi as Marquis of Zhuiji, Lü Fen as Marquis of Lücheng, and also enfeoffed five chancellors as marquises.
呂媭 is Lü Xu (Empress Lü's sister), not Lü Kui.

Empress Lü wished to make Lü clan kings. She first established Emperor Xiaohui's rear palace son Qiang as the King of Huaiyang, son Buyi as the King of Changshan, son Shan as Lord Xiangcheng, son Zhao as Lord Zhi, son Wu as Lord Huguan.

Empress Lü wished to make Lü clan kings. She first established Emperor Xiaohui's rear palace son Qiang as the King of Huaiyang, son Buyi as the King of Changshan, son Shan as Lord Xiangcheng, son Chao as Lord Zhi, son Wu as Lord Huguan.
子朝 is Chao (朝), not Zhao.

Some of his ministers secretly brought him food, but each time they were seized and punished. Starving, the King of Zhao sang, "The Lu clan rules, and the Liu house is in peril; they threaten kings and marquises, and force one of their women on me as consort.
